question.text: Ganga Capital is bidding INR 1,000 crore enterprise value for TargetCo with forecast Year-1 EBITDA of INR 125 crore. The fund plans: (a) INR 700 crore senior debt at 11% (6-yr amortising), (b) INR 150 crore mezzanine at 14% PIK, (c) INR 150 crore equity. What is the entry EV/EBITDA multiple and the total debt/EBITDA leverage at close?

explanation.text: The Logic: EV/EBITDA = 1,000 / 125 = 8.0x. Total debt = Senior 700 + Mezzanine 150 = 850 crore, so debt/EBITDA = 850 / 125 = 6.8x. This uses the workbook's definition of enterprise value and EV/EBITDA as an enterprise-value multiple. The Trap: Option B understates the EV calculation. Option C overstates EV at 10x against the stated INR 1,000 crore. Option D correctly computes EV but wrongly excludes mezzanine from total debt, even though mezzanine financing is debt for leverage-ratio purposes. Note: LBO/private credit context is on pages 209-210, EV and EV/EBITDA are defined on pages 256-266 and LBO/mezzanine appear in the glossary on page 398; the workbook does not state a mid-market norm or covenant-package prescription for this leverage level.
